 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V. Act') by the claimants challenging the judgment and award passed by Principal M.A.C.T and Chief Judge, Court of Small causes, Bengaluru, in MVC No.2843/2011 dated 28.11.2012.
2.

entities.text: Chief Judge, Court of Small causes, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the case are as under:
NC: 2023:KHC:41179 On 06.06.2010 Narayanappa was sitting in a Tractor- Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-06-A-8259 and KA-06-A-8260 and the driver of the said Tractor drove it in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the Tractor-Trailer capsized and Narayanappa sustained fatal injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Baptist hospital Hebbal, Bengaluru, but he succumbed in the hospital due to the injuries on 10.06.2010.

The deceased was working as a loader and unloader in the said Tractor-Trailer and earning Rs.300/-
per day.

The petitioners are the dependants and have lost the bread earner and hence, they filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents.
3. Respondent No.1-Insurance company filed objection statement denying the age, occupation of the deceased and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tractor-Trailer.

It is admitted that, the Tractor-Trailer was covered with the policy, but it is asserted that the driver did not possess Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65402306/
2 any valid and NC: 2023:KHC:41179 effective driving license.

entities.text: Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further asserted that, the deceased was traveling as a gratuitous passenger in the Tractor-Trailer and hence, the Insurance company- respondent No.1 disputed their liability.
4. The 2nd respondent filed objection statement by denying the allegations and the said assertions made there under.

He has simply submitted that, he was the owner of the Tractor-Trailer and he had sold it to the 3rd respondent by handing over the original documents as well as possession and hence, he asserts that he is not responsible for payment of compensation.

The 3rd respondent,
though represented by the counsel did not choose to contest the matter.

5. The Tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the petition-in-part by awarding a total compensation of Rs.4,26,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum by fastening the liability on respondent No.3-owner holding that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger.
Being aggrieved by this judgment and award the appellants/claimants are before this Court by way of this appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurer.
8.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 though served are unrepresented.
9. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants would contend that the claimants are the wife and son of the deceased and they are the dependents.

It is also asserted that, the deceased Narayanappa was working as a loader and unloader in the Tractor-Trailer which is evident from the allegations made in the complaint as well as the statement given under Section 161 by the witnesses before the investigating officer.
Hence, he would contend that the Tribunal has erred in holding that, he is a gratuitous passenger and fastening the liability on the NC: 2023:KHC:41179 owner.

It is further asserted that, the compensation awarded by taking the notional income on the lower side and it requires enhancement and no proper compensation was awarded under the head of 'loss of consortium'.
Hence, it is prayed for enhancement of the compensation by fastening the liability on respondent No.1-Insurer.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurer would contend that, all the three respondents are represented by their respective counsels and respondent No.3, who claims to be the owner did not file any objection statement nor lead any evidence asserting that the deceased was a loader and unloader working under him.

He would invite the attention of the Court to Ex.R3 wherein, there is reference regarding fall from the Tractor-Trailer alone and in the given facts and circumstances, the owner or the driver of the offending Tractor-Trailer would have been the best witnesses to say whether the deceased was a loader and unloader employed by respondent No.3.

He would also invite NC: 2023:KHC:41179 attention of the Court regarding Ex.P3 where there is Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65402306/
3 reference that the deceased was intoxicated.

entities.text: Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he would contend that, the Tribunal was justified in fastening the liability on respondent No.3 and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

11. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, there is no serious dispute of the fact that deceased Narayanappa suffered accidental injuries and succumbed because of the accidental injuries.

It is the specific contention of the claimants that he was working as a coolie in the Tractor-Trailer belonging to respondent No.3, but the said fact is not asserted by respondent No.3,
who was the owner of the offending Tractor-Trailer.
Even respondent No.3 though appeared through his counsel did not file any objection statement nor contested the matter.
Even before this Court, though he was served, he is unrepresented.
Apart from that, he has not even challenged the judgment and award pertaining to liability fastened on him.

No attempt has been made by the NC:
2023:KHC:41179 claimants to examine the driver or the owner i.e respondent No.3 to substantiate the contention that the deceased was working as loader and unloader in the offending Tractor-Trailer.
12. Learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance on a decision in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. SRI.MARUTHI AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2011 KAR 4139

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. SRI.MARUTHI AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2011 KAR 4139
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the facts and circumstances of the said case are entirely different.

Apart from that, in the said reported case, the vehicle in question was a goods vehicle and the charge sheet itself clearly establishes that the deceased was working as a loader and unloader in the goods vehicle.
But in the instant case, the charge sheet does not disclose as to whether the deceased was working as a loader or unloader.
Hence, the contention of the appellants/claimants that the deceased was working as loader/unloader holds no water.

As per the claimants and as per the criminal Court records in the form of charge sheet and other documents, the accident has occurred on 06.06.2010 and the deceased was immediately shifted to Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru on the same day at 3.40 pm i.e within one hour forty minutes, but Ex.R3 and Ex.R4 are the records pertaining to Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru wherein, the date of admission is shown as 07.06.2010 at 3.40 pm.

The history given was, fall from the Tractor today i.e.
on 07.06.2010 at 2.00 pm in Bandikodigehalli Village and there is also a reference that the patient was under the influence of alcohol and Ex.R4 is the another document pertaining to Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru wherein, there is also a reference regarding admission on 07.06.2010 on account of accident on the same day at 2.00 pm, but the claim made by the claimants is in respect of accident dated 06.06.2010.
These anomalies are not at all explained.

There is no dispute of the fact that, respondent No.2 was initially owner of the offending Tractor-Trailer, but from Ex.R2, it is evident that he had transferred the vehicle by way of sale in favour of respondent No.3 and from 26.08.2009, respondent No.3 was the owner of the offending Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65402306/
4 vehicle.

entities.text: Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.3 though represented by the counsel did not dispute this aspect regarding his ownership and even he did not assert that the deceased Narayanappa was a loader working under him.

Considering these facts and circumstances, the Principal enunciated in the decision reported in SRI.MARUTHI AND OTHERS referred supra cannot be made applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case in hand, in view of the fact that, in the said case there was material evidence on record in the charge sheet itself regarding the deceased working as a coolie, but in the instant case, no such evidence is forthcoming.
Hence, the Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability on respondent No.3- owner.
Admittedly the accident has occurred on 06.06.2010.
The Tribunal has taken the monthly notional income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- pm.
This Court is consistently taking the notional income in respect of the accidents that occurred in the year 2010 at Rs.5,500/- pm.
The deceased was aged about 51 years.
The deceased was having two dependants and hence, 1/3rd is required to be deducted.
Since the deceased was self employee, 10% is required to be added towards future prospects.
Hence, his monthly income would be Rs.5,500+550=6,050/-.
Hence, the monthly income of the deceased is required to be taken at Rs.6,050/-.
Since the deceased was aged about 51 years, the multiplier 11 is applicable.
Further out of Rs.6,050/-, 1/3rd is required to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Hence loss of dependency would work out at Rs.6,050 x 12 x 11 x 2/3 =
Rs.5,32,400/-.

Hence, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of a sum of Rs.5,32,400/-
under the head 'loss of dependency'.

Further, claimant No.1 is the widow and claimant No.2 is the son and both are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of consortium' and hence, the claimants would be entitled for Rs.80,000/- under the head of 'loss of consortium'.
They are also entitled for Rs.15,000/- under the head of 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- under the head of 'funeral expenses'.

Hence claimants,
would be entitled for a total compensation under the various heads as under:
SL.No. Particulars Amount  1 Loss of dependency Rs.5,32,400/-
 2 Loss of consortium Rs.80,000/-
 3 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 4 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 Enhanced compensation Rs.6,42,400/-
Smt Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65402306/
5

entities.text: Gangamma vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the claimants fail to prove that the deceased was a loader, and respondent No.3 did not assert it, he being the owner is liable to pay the entire compensation with accrued interest.

Hence,
claimants would be entitled - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41179 for total compensation of Rs.6,42,400/- as against Rs.4,26,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
As such, the appeal needs to be allowed in part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1.
The appeal is allowed in part.
2. The claimants are held entitled for a total compensation of Rs.6,42,400/- as against Rs.4,26,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

3. The enhanced compensation of Rs.2,16,400/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the realization.
4.
Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the entire enhanced compensation with interest thereon within a period of six weeks.
The appeal as against respondent Nos.1 and 2 stands dismissed.
